Look up a company's CNPJ by name

Source: R/util-cnpj.R
cnpj_lookup.Rd

Searches the CVM company registers for a name, or part of one, and returns the matching registrations with their CNPJ. Use it to find the cnpj that cvm_fetch() takes. The function never picks a company for you: it lists every match, and you choose.

Usage

cnpj_lookup(name, source = NULL)

Arguments

name

A single string: the company name, or part of it.

source

One of "mirror" or "cvm", as in cvm_fetch(). NULL (default) resolves to the active backend via cvm_source_get().

Value

A tibble with one row per registration: cnpj_cia, denom_social, denom_comerc, cd_cvm, sit, dt_reg, dt_cancel and table (the register the row comes from). Rows the CVM repeats per market (tp_merc) appear once. Active registrations (no dt_cancel) come first, then by denom_social. No match returns zero rows and a message.

Details

The search reads the three registers of the cad dataset (companhias, estrangeiras and incentivadas, see cvm_tables()) from source and looks for name in denom_social and denom_comerc. Every word of name must appear, in any order, ignoring case and accents: "banco brasil" finds "BANCO DO BRASIL S.A." and "tiete" finds "AES TIETÊ ENERGIA S.A". Words are matched as plain text, not as regular expressions.

Cancelled registrations are included, after the active ones: a delisted company has no ticker, which is when a CNPJ is most needed. The registers hold today's names only; a company that changed its name is found by the current one.

See also

cvm_fetch(), whose cnpj argument takes the result; its ticker argument is the shortcut for exchange-listed companies.

Other utilities: cnpj_clean(), cnpj_format(), cvm_tbl

Examples

# \donttest{
hits <- cnpj_lookup("magazine luiza")
